newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy says committed to telecoms liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: Italy says committed to telecoms liberalisation.

text.p: Italy's Posts Ministry said it had asked three main state-linked telecommunications companies on Wednesday to respect undertakings with the European Union to liberalise the industry.

A statement said Minister Antonio Maccanico had also told the companies at a meeting that he planned to allow a supercordless DECT telephone service to operate under equal conditions for all providers.
The meeting was with the managing directors of Stet, Telecom Italia SpA and mobile telephone operator TIM.
"The managing directors of the three companies expressed the common intention of working to follow the objectives indicated by the minister," the statement said.

European Commission sources said earlier in Brussels that Commissioner Karel Van Miert had called on Italy to implement measures aimed at creating equal conditions in the digital GSM mobile telephone market.
They said Van Miert had written to Prime Minister Romano Prodi asking him to fix a precise date for the introduction of the changes, which the Commission drew up in October 1995.
The measures were meant to be introduced by the Italian government in January to establish a fair market for Italy's second mobile phone group Omnitel.
Omnitel, an international consortium controlled by Olivetti, launched its GSM service in December 1995 to compete with TIM.
"The Minister, in what was also a response to the requests by Commissioner Van Miert, sought assurances that the commitments made would be respected," the ministry statement said.

It said that on DECT (Digital European Cordless Telephony), Maccanico had said Italy intended the service to be launched "in a framework that guarantees effective equality among all operators and concrete respect for the principle of free competition in the sector."
Fixed line telecoms operator Telecom Italia announced plans last October to launch a DECT service.

The announcement sparked controversy when anti-trust authority chairman Giuliano Amato said that if it went ahead it would be taking advantage of Telecom's dominant position in the fixed-line market and compete with mobile phone operators.
TIM, Telecom Italia's sister company, is also seeking authorisation to offer a DECT cordless service, while Omnitel has asked for authorisation to experiment with DECT technology.
